question.:question/problem: Which of the following is an upper triangular matrix?
question.:question/worked-solution:
Notice that $B$ is a matrix for which all entries *below* the diagonal are $0$'s:

$$
B=\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{bmatrix}
$$

Hence, it is an upper triangular matrix. 

By contrast, matrices $A$, $C$, $D$, and $E$ each have at least one non-zero entry below the diagonal:

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}-2 & 0 \\ -11 & -2\end{bmatrix}
$$

$$
C=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 0 \\ -11 & 0\end{bmatrix}
$$

$$
D=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 \\ -11 & 1\end{bmatrix}
$$

$$
E=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 0 \\ -11 & 2\end{bmatrix}
$$

So, they are not upper triangular matrices.
